# Design — causal-loop-diagram ## Overview A module at `src/diagrams/causal-loop/` drawing `.cld` documents under the origin `systems/causal-loop-diagram`: variables joined by polarised causal links, with the cycles those links form enumerated, labelled `R` or `B` by arithmetic rather than by assertion, and arranged on demand by a self-organizing layout that has been made deterministic. Three things make this module unlike its siblings, and the design is mostly about them: 1. **Its central claim is about cycles.** Every other diagram in the catalog draws hierarchy, containment or sequence. This one draws feedback, and a feedback loop is a property of the whole graph rather than of any element in it. That puts a cycle enumerator on the read path and gives the module a class of finding no sibling has. 2. **A loop has no position of its own.** It is a set of links, drawn where its members are. It therefore joins links in the category of things the viewport must filter *structurally*, and it is the second reason this module cannot use a position as a proxy for existence. 3. **Its layout is a neural method with a determinism problem.** Meyer's self-organizing graphs are stochastic by construction. Requirement 6 keeps the method and removes the stochasticity, and this document says exactly where each source of randomness goes. ## Steering Document Alignment ### Technical Standards (tech.md) - **Files are the source of truth.** The `.cld` body is plain diffable text; authored positions go in the `.adp` registration's `layout:` block, never into the body — the rule tech.md states for a format that carries no layout of its own. - **The backend owns the filesystem.** The client reads and writes nothing; every change travels as a command and comes back as a delta. - **Virtualization is view-driven.** The whole document is laid out and the viewport filters the result. ### Project Structure (structure.md) `src/diagrams/causal-loop/` with `backend/`, `api/` and `client/`. Backend holds `EtAlii.Adp.Diagram.CausalLoop` and `EtAlii.Adp.Diagram.CausalLoop.Tests`; `_Model/` and `Commands/` stay in the project's own namespace. Examples live in the module and are copied into `src/examples/`. ## Code Reuse Analysis ### Existing components to leverage - **`IDiagramSession`, `DiagramDelta`, `DiagramAddDelta`, `DiagramRemoveDelta`, `DiagramViewport`** — the delta vocabulary, unextended. This module adds no delta kind. - **`IDiagramDocumentFactory`** — registered, per Requirement 5.1, because a `HasDocumentSibling` module without one cannot create a document at all. - **`RegistrationLayout` and `SetRegistrationLayoutCommand`** — authored positions and their byte-restoring inverse. No new persistence mechanism. - **`viewReportOf`, `useViewReport`, `shownRectOf`** — the client half of the view-delta loop, taken whole. A guard fails a module that builds its own. - **`canvas.css` and its nineteen `canvas-*` classes**, the shared `connections/` components (`bezier` for the curved causal link, `straight` where a link is short) and `elements/` (`ellipse` or `span` for a variable, which in this notation is a label rather than a box), plus `CanvasScrollbars` and `scrollExtentOf`. - **`IContextActionProvider`, `IContextPropertyProvider`, `ContextPropertyDefinition`** — menus and grid through the standard paths. - **The drawn-element budget precedent** — a bounded view with an honest banner, as the RDF family established. ### Integration points - **The catalog** — a row in `docs/diagrams.md`, which has none today. - **`.gitattributes`** — `*.cld -text` if and only if the tests byte-compare documents, by extension and never by directory. ### What the shared canvas does *not* offer, stated because Requirement 9 forbids the private workaround There is **no shared thickness abstraction** to reuse. The only `thickness` in the tree is a local in `C4Layout` meaning a rank's depth, which is unrelated. Line weight in the shared canvas is `stroke-width` in `canvas.css`, and it offers effectively two visible widths (1.5 and 2.5) plus a wide invisible hit area. That matters because Requirement 8.2 makes a link's **weight** editable. The design consequence is deliberate: **weight maps to a small ordered set of shared classes, not to a continuous stroke width.** A weight is an author's annotation, not a measurement, so a coarse ladder is honest about what it is. If the ladder needs a step the shared stylesheet does not have, the step is added **to the shared stylesheet** and becomes available to every module — adding a module-private appearance file is the thing Requirement 9.1 exists to prevent, and five modules already carry 104–261 lines of exactly that. ## Architecture ```mermaid graph TD A[".cld body"] --> B[CausalLoopParser] B --> C[CausalLoopModel
variables, links, loops] C --> D[CycleFinder
Johnson, bounded] D --> E[LoopPolarity
even negatives = R] C --> F[CausalLoopLayout
computed default] C --> G[CausalLoopValidator] E --> G F --> H[CausalLoopElementMapper] C --> H E --> H H --> I[CausalLoopSession
Baseline, UpdateView] J[".adp layout: block"] --> H K[SelfOrganizingLayout
invoked action] --> J ``` The read path is one direction: parse, model, find cycles, derive polarity, lay out, map, filter, send. The self-organizing layout is not on it — it is an action that writes authored positions and lets the ordinary path redraw. ## Components and Interfaces ### Backend: the document and its model - **`CausalLoopDocument`** — the parsed lines, positions preserved, so a writer can splice rather than reserialize. - **`CausalLoopParser` → `CausalLoopModel`** — variables, links and loops. - **`CausalLoopLink`** — `From`, `To`, `Polarity` (`Positive` | `Negative` | `Unstated`), `Delayed`, `Weight`, `Label`. `Unstated` is a real case and Requirement 3.6 turns on it: a link with no polarity makes every loop through it undecidable, and inventing `Positive` as a default would fabricate an answer. - **`CausalLoopLoop`** — `Identifier` (`R1`, `B2`), `Name`, and the member links. Note what it does not have: a position. ### Backend: cycles and polarity — the module's own reason to exist - **`CycleFinder`** — Johnson's elementary cycles algorithm over the link graph, which is the standard enumerator and the one AutoCLD uses for this exact purpose. Bounded per Requirement 3.5: a maximum cycle count, and when the bound is reached the reader is told how many were examined rather than the check silently doing less than it claims. - **`LoopPolarity`** — the even/odd rule, and nothing more: reinforcing where the count of `Negative` links is even, balancing where odd, undecidable where any member link is `Unstated`. - The stated label and the computed one are **kept separate all the way to the grid and the problems panel**. Requirement 3.3 forbids silent correction because the author's label may be the intent and the arrows the mistake; a design that overwrote one with the other would make that impossible to see. ### Backend: the writers Each edit is an `ICommand` with a byte-restoring inverse, spliced into the document rather than reserialized: - `AddVariableCommand`, `RenameVariableCommand`, `RemoveVariableCommand` - `AddLinkCommand`, `SetLinkPolarityCommand`, `SetLinkDelayCommand`, `SetLinkWeightCommand`, `RemoveLinkCommand` - `AddLoopCommand`, `SetLoopNameCommand`, `SetLoopMembershipCommand`, `RemoveLoopCommand` Requirement 4.4 has a consequence worth naming: **removing a loop removes the loop statement and not its links.** A link belongs to the diagram; the loop is a claim about a path through it. The inverse restores the loop statement alone. ### Backend: the self-organizing layout `SelfOrganizingLayout` implements Meyer's self-organizing graphs — competitive learning extended from Kohonen's self-organizing map, where the neighbourhood is measured in **graph** distance rather than in layout distance, which is what makes it a graph layout rather than a clustering. The method has three sources of randomness. Each is replaced, and the replacements are the whole of Requirement 6.2: | Source in the published method | What this design uses instead | | --- | --- | | Random initial node positions | A phyllotaxis spiral seeded by each variable's index in the document's stable order — a pure function of the document | | A random stimulus sequence | A fixed-length low-discrepancy sequence over the layout rectangle, computed from the iteration index alone | | Arbitrary tie-breaking for the best-matching unit | The stable document order | Plus a fixed iteration count, and a learning-rate and neighbourhood-radius schedule that is a function of the iteration index and nothing else. No wall-clock, no RNG, no settling animation whose stopping point depends on timing. **A converged self-organizing map does not guarantee non-overlap, and Requirement 6.5 does.** So the layout is two phases: 1. the self-organizing pass, which decides the *arrangement* — related variables near, unrelated apart; 2. a bounded, deterministic **separation pass** that pushes overlapping boxes apart in stable order for a fixed number of rounds. If overlaps remain when the rounds are exhausted, the action **refuses for that document and reports the size at which it failed**, per Requirement 6.7. That is the honest outcome, and it is the reason the ratio bound is not the guard here: a hairball is roughly square and would pass an extent-ratio check comfortably while being exactly the failure the ruling names. On success the positions are written through `SetRegistrationLayoutCommand`, so the arrangement is one undo away like every other edit. ### Backend: mapping, and two things without positions `CausalLoopElementMapper` produces elements for variables, links and loop labels. Two of those three have no position of their own: - a **link** is drawn between its endpoints; - a **loop label** is drawn at the centroid of its members. Both are therefore filtered **structurally** — a link when both endpoints survive the viewport, a loop label when enough of its members do — and never by testing a position they do not have. Requirement 7.1 forbids the `(0, 0)` fallback that four modules shipped and a viewport then culled everywhere except the top-left corner. ### Backend: validation `CausalLoopValidator` reports, and never corrects: - a loop whose stated label disagrees with the computed polarity — naming the loop, the stated label and the computed one (Requirement 3.3); - a cycle the document labels not at all (Requirement 3.4), which is the finding this notation most exists to produce; - a loop rendered undecidable by a link with no stated polarity (Requirement 3.6); - the cycle bound having been reached, with the count examined (Requirement 3.5). ### Client - **`CausalLoopCanvas`** — shared `canvas-*` classes and `canvas.css`, shared `CanvasScrollbars`, shared bezier connections with `.canvas-arrowhead`. Variables draw as labels rather than boxes, which is the notation's own convention. Polarity is drawn at the arrowhead end; a delay draws as the conventional strokes across the link; a loop label draws its `R`/`B` identifier and name at its centroid. - **`useCausalLoopStream`** — the delta stream, plus `reportView` built with the shared `viewReportOf` on the client it already holds. - The property grid contributes variable labels, and for a link its weight, polarity and delay; for a loop, its identifier, name, computed polarity and the stated one where they differ. ## Data Models ### The body format, and why not XMILE Requirement 1.2 requires this decision recorded with reasons. **XMILE was considered and is not adopted.** It is the OASIS interchange standard for system dynamics and it is genuinely the established format in this domain, which is exactly why it was weighed. It is rejected on three grounds: 1. **It is a model format, and a causal loop diagram is not a model.** XMILE carries stocks, flows, equations and simulation specifications. A CLD states none of them. Adopting it would mean shipping documents that are overwhelmingly absent, in a format whose readers reasonably expect to be able to run them. 2. **It has no first-class representation for the thing this notation is about.** The `R`/`B` loop labelling, with an identifier and a name, is the CLD's central artifact and is not an XMILE concept. It would have to be smuggled through annotations, at which point the standard is carrying none of the weight. 3. **The extension the user fixed is `.cld`.** An XMILE payload under a `.cld` extension is a third spelling of a format that already has two (`.xmile`, `.stmx`), and helps nobody. The body is therefore this module's own **line-oriented text format**: one statement per line, so adding a link is a one-line diff (Requirement 1.3), and readable without a tool. Its exact grammar is a task-level decision; the constraints it must meet are Requirement 1.3 and Requirement 4.1's splice discipline. Converting a `.cld` to XMILE — the stock-and-flow step the literature documents — remains a non-goal and a plausible future specification. Nothing here forecloses it. ### The wire A `causal-loop.proto` in `api/` carrying a variable payload, a link payload (polarity, delay, weight, label) and a loop payload (identifier, name, computed polarity, stated polarity). Proto message names take the `Proto` suffix where they would otherwise collide with a backend model type, per the azure-pipeline precedent. ## Error Handling ### Error scenarios - **An unparseable document** — the diagram reports that it cannot be read, naming the line, and draws nothing rather than drawing a partial graph that misleads. - **A link naming a variable the document never declares** — a finding, and the link is not drawn, because an arrow to nothing is worse than an absent arrow. - **A loop naming a link the document does not state** — a finding naming the loop; the loop is not drawn. - **A cycle count beyond the bound** — the banner states what was examined. - **The self-organizing layout failing to separate** — refused with the size, per Requirement 6.7, never a hairball delivered quietly. - **An edit against a stale element id** — refused with the standard sentence; the same sentence wherever that refusal is reachable. ## Testing Strategy ### Unit testing - `LoopPolarity` against the even/odd rule, zero negatives included, since zero being even is the case a reader most often gets wrong. - `CycleFinder` on a graph with nested and overlapping cycles, and on one with none. - The determinism of `SelfOrganizingLayout`: the same document laid out twice yields identical positions, and — the stronger test — laid out in **two different processes** yields identical positions, since a same-process comparison would pass against a cached result. - The separation pass: no two boxes intersect after it, at the budget's full size. - Each command's inverse restoring the document byte for byte. - Every sweep over a projected collection asserts the collection is non-empty first, so no guard here can pass vacuously. ### Integration testing - A registered document opens: variables, links and loop labels stream, and the `.adp`'s authored positions overlay the computed ones. - A view change produces deltas — asserted in the **backend**, because a client-side assertion that `reportView` was called passes against a session that answers with nothing. - The self-organizing action writes positions and one undo restores the registration byte for byte. - A document whose stated label disagrees with its arrows produces the Requirement 3.3 finding, with both labels named. ### End-to-end testing `tests.md` entries: a diagram whose `R2` is arithmetically balancing shows the disagreement without the document changing; a delayed link draws its strokes and reads correctly in the grid; the self-organizing action rearranges a tangled diagram and one undo puts it back exactly.
